newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil lower house to vote re-election amendments.
newsitem.headline: Brazil lower house to vote re-election amendments.

text.p: Brazil's lower house will start voting at 1100 local (1300 GMT) on a series of a amendments to a bill allowing presidential re-election, an official said.

The government has said it will try to defeat all the proposed changes to the constitutional amendment on re-election, approved by the Chamber of Deputies in a stunning victory for President Fernando Henrique Cardoso Tuesday night.
The amendments include a proposal that incumbent presidents, governors and mayors resign six months before elections and a proposal to tie re-election to a plebiscite or a referendum.
The government must muster a three-fifth majority, or 308 of the Chamber's 513 votes, in order to defeat each amendment.
On Tuesday night, the government won 336 votes in favour of re-election. Most opponents of the bill did not vote.
